summary: Adopt only as the required Node transport beneath axios. 1.16.2 is a small, zero-dependency, MIT-licensed redirect implementation with recent releases and no recorded advisories. It has no npm provenance, so pin 1.16.2 exactly and record the gap; it is not a browser client and not a standalone replacement for axios.
reasoning: Role is transitive: the request identifies follow-redirects as part of the axios stack, where it is reached through axios rather than imported by application code. It is not a candidate for the browser/Node HTTP client role itself.
The full axios runtime tree was installed and verified: follow-redirects 1.16.2 is the only confirmed axios edge in this batch, and the tree is 27 MIT packages with no install scripts.
Footprint is minimal: 0 runtime dependencies, a 31 KB unpacked package, and no preinstall/install/postinstall hooks. It adds no transitive tree or install-time execution to axios.
Security surface as recorded: OSV returns no advisories for 1.16.2, and the axios tree audit reports zero vulnerabilities.
Maintenance is active: 1.16.2 was published 2026-10-25, the repository was pushed 2026-10-25, it is not archived, and 73 versions have been published by two npm maintainers.

Release integrity is the gap: npm_provenance is false and no npm attestation was found. The requirement explicitly permits this only with exact version pinning and a recorded gap; axios must pin or lock follow-redirects 1.16.2.
Packaging is Node-only and CJS-only, which is correct for the axios Node adapter. It does not need to satisfy the browser half of the requirement because axios supplies the browser adapter.
The 93.9M weekly downloads are not treated as a quality signal; they include CI and transitive installs.
caveats: No npm attestation for 1.16.2. Pin 1.16.2 exactly and re-check provenance on each upgrade.
CI publishing was not audited. If a future review finds manual publishing without a controlled workflow, the release-integrity verdict should drop.
Node-only and CJS-only. Do not present it as a browser HTTP client or as a replacement for axios.
No bundled TypeScript declarations. The requirement does not require types for this transitive package, but TypeScript consumers of follow-redirects directly would need their own declarations.
Two npm maintainers and 21 open issues; responsiveness to a future advisory depends on the small maintainer team.
Install size was not separately measured; the 31 KB unpacked figure is the package itself, not its contribution to a bundle.
The 93.9M weekly downloads include CI and transitive traffic and are not evidence of direct adoption.
